implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines supplies the queue: Channel<T> is the coroutine analogue of BlockingQueue with a suspending send instead of a blocking put and a suspending receive instead of take, produce{} builds the producer side, consumeEach or a for loop drains the receiver, and close ends the stream deterministically. What replaces the classic structure is the channel plus structured concurrency - the drain lives in its own coroutine and cancellation propagates, so no stop flag is needed. A plain ArrayDeque with an explicit drain remains the better fit for single-threaded UI or game code.
pitfalls: send suspends once the buffer is full, so an undisciplined producer can stall its own coroutine chain - use trySend or an explicit overflow policy for fire-and-forget senders.
A channel left open keeps its collector coroutine suspended forever; close the producer side (or cancel the scope) so the drain terminates.
consumeEach cancels the underlying channel when its consumer completes, so it must not be used for fan-out - iterate with a for loop when several consumers share the channel.
